newsitem.title: USA: U.S. crudes retrench, grades ease in thin session.
newsitem.headline: U.S. crudes retrench, grades ease in thin session.

text.p: U.S. cash crudes continued weaker Wednesday afternoon, pressured by negative inventory reports and technical consolidation.
Cash grade barrels found little interest from refiners, keeping a lid on the number of confirmed trades. A Shell-sponsored shippers meeting thinned the number of market participants, traders noted.
June West Texas Intermediate/Cushing lost ground from morning price levels, and was currently talked around 35 cents lower at $20.95-21.05 a barrel.

June/July spreads were stagnant, favoring July by a two to three cents premium. June WTI/Cushing rolls deflated on the return of a July premium, selling at $2.04 and talked now below the $2.00 barometer.
Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James sold at six cents over the benchmark, and talked at premiums of 5-10 cents.
Midland/WTI sold at WTI/Cushing -33 cents, steady from recent ranges. Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire was valued at a 35 cents discount, with no fresh trades recorded.
Sour barrels remained at unchanged price levels, finding only nominal interest for moving barrels.

Exchange for physicals (EFP's) retreated a few pennies to sell at plus seven cents from highs at plus 11-13 cents on Tuesday. Traders said EFP's were underpinned by expectations for re-delivery of foreign crudes against June paper matches, leaving many nervous players looking to secure WTI barrels.
